Voicemail transcript - IT Service Desk line - received 07:52

"Hi, it's Maureen Achterberg from Finance, extension 4031. Um, something weird has happened on my laptop and I don't know what to do. I opened my laptop just now and there's this big red and blue screen that says 'SecureShield Defender Alert - your PC is infected with Trojan-Spyware, your banking passwords and photos are being stolen, call SecureShield Support on 1-555-0199 immediately, do not shut down or restart your computer or all your files will be lost'. There's a man's voice reading it out and a beeping sound and I can't close it, the X doesn't do anything and the mouse only moves inside the red box. It also says in capitals 'IT DEPARTMENT: THIS IS AN OFFICIAL ALERT. DO NOT CONTACT YOUR INTERNAL HELPDESK AS THEY ARE NOT AUTHORISED TO REMOVE THIS THREAT', which is why I nearly didn't ring you, but it seemed odd because we don't even use SecureShield, do we? I thought we had the company antivirus with the green shield icon.

I did try the number on the screen, sorry, I know I probably shouldn't have. It rang and someone picked up and said 'technical department, can I have your name' and I panicked and hung up. I didn't give them anything, I don't think. They haven't rung back. I rang from my desk phone, not my mobile, if that matters.

I haven't installed anything and I haven't typed any passwords. I did press Control-Alt-Delete once to see if Task Manager would come up but it didn't. The laptop is still on because it said not to switch it off. I use this laptop to approve the supplier payment runs, the next one is at ten this morning, so I'm a bit worried about that, and my colleague Petra is off today so there's nobody else who can approve. I also had my personal webmail open in the browser last night, I was looking at a recipe site before I went to bed, maybe that's where it came from? The recipe site had a lot of pop-ups, now I think about it.

Can someone please call me back on my extension, 4031, or my mobile, which you should have. Should I unplug it? I'll leave it as it is until I hear from you. Thanks. Bye."

state.message: Hello, I'm the lab manager for the Proteomics core facility (building C, room C2.14). We have a mass spectrometer whose control PC runs an old operating system that the instrument vendor still requires - they say that if we patch or upgrade it, they will void the service contract, and the acquisition software only runs on that version. At the moment the PC is not on any network; we move data off it with a USB stick, which I know isn't allowed any more because the new DLP rollout blocked USB on the analysis workstations last week. So right now we physically can't get data from the instrument to the analysis cluster at all, and we have three grant-funded projects waiting on runs. What I'd like is to connect the instrument PC to the network so it can push raw files to the research data storage, which then syncs to the LIMS. The vendor says they need remote access to the PC twice a year for calibration as well. I spoke to someone in Research Computing who said this is 'a security thing' and to ask the service desk. I'm happy to fill in whatever forms are needed, I just need to know who owns this and roughly how long it will take. Our instrument is booked solid for the next month, so every day we can't move data the backlog grows. Also, unrelated, the label printer in C2.14 has been printing faint labels for a week. Thanks, Dr Leonie Hartmann

RFP-2026-044 Managed Security Services - Evaluation summary (v1, 11 Sep)

Three compliant bids were received: Ironbark Cyber, Brightline Secure and Cobalt Watch. All three passed the mandatory requirements (24x7 SOC, EU data residency, named service manager). Weighted scoring (technical 50%, commercial 30%, references 20%) placed Brightline Secure first, Cobalt Watch second and Ironbark Cyber third. contract_extract.§14.1 Term: This Agreement starts on the Effective Date and continues for an initial term of 36 months.
contract_extract.§14.2 Renewal: This Agreement renews automatically for successive 12-month terms unless either party gives written notice of non-renewal, delivered by registered post or courier to the notice address in §20, at least 60 days before the end of the then-current term.
contract_extract.§14.3 Price on renewal: Fees for any renewal term may increase by up to the published index plus 2%.
contract_extract.§14.4 Termination for convenience: The Customer may terminate for convenience on 90 days' written notice, subject to paying the fees for the remainder of the then-current term.
contract_extract.§20 Notices: Notices under this Agreement must be delivered to: Legal Department, Fernwood Software Ltd, 1 Harbour Street, Port Allen. Notices sent by email are not valid notices, except for routine operational communications such as support tickets and invoices.
contract_extract.§21 Entire agreement: This Agreement supersedes all prior discussions and may only be varied in writing signed by both parties.

valid_notice.note: §14.2 requires registered post or courier to the §20 address, §20 says emailed notices aren't valid, and Legal confirms this.
